scenario.question: We move to combat and declare ALL TEN of our creatures as attackers against seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 17 life): Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3), Hanweir Garrison (2/3), General Kreat, the Boltbringer (2/2), five 1/1 Human Tokens and two 1/1 Goblin Tokens. We then activate Goblin Burrows once. seat-2 has TWO creatures — Reclamation Sage (2/1) untapped and Splinterfright (*/*) TAPPED. (a) Resolve every attack trigger in Comprehensive Rules order and state the total power attacking seat-2 and the non-combat damage dealt to it. (b) Is seat-2 dead before our end step, taking the most favourable block available to it? Cite the rule that decides whether Splinterfright can block.
notes: RE-LIFTED ON A FIXED BRIDGE (2026-09-28). The first lift of this board (stack 008, now superseded) omitted THREE things a rules-checker then found: seat-2's Splinterfright, and two of our Goblin Tokens. Declared power was reported as 12 and is 14; seat-2 had one recorded blocker and has two.

SPLINTERFRIGHT IS TAPPED, and that is now a FIELD ON THE BOARD rather than an argument the artifact had to make. Its power is `*/*` because the log does not carry a characteristic-defining value — treat its size as unknown and say what that means for the answer.

THE ACTIONS ARE AUTHORED. Forge's AI did not attack here: it blocked on three of the next four turns and Zada died before turn 31. The question is what a pilot would have done with the board the AI was handed.

A creature on this board has a CHARACTERISTIC-DEFINING power (`*/*`): the log prints no value, and the graveyard lists in this artifact are BATTLEFIELD DEATHS ONLY — a milled or discarded card never appears as a zone change — so its size is UNKNOWN and must not be computed from here. The resolution below shows the answer does not depend on it.

steps.action: Set the frame and state the provenance. Turn 27, precombat main, we hold priority. Life: us 5, seat-2 (jarad-graveyard) 17, seat-3 (abaddon) 36, seat-4 (sythis-enchantress) 41 (scenario-facts drain_arithmetic: 3 opponents, per-opponent life 17 / 36 / 41, opposing life total 94). We move to combat, so any kill must land in the combat damage step of the combat phase, which precedes the postcombat main phase and the ending phase that holds our end step. BOARD PROVENANCE: the slug is goblin-storm@zada-v1 and scenario-facts card_membership.NOT_IN_THE_DECK names Hanweir Garrison. Hanweir Garrison is the engine of this line, so THE LINE IS REACHABLE ON THE zada-v1 BRANCH LIST ONLY and NOT on goblin-storm's sleeved 99. Boggart Shenanigans, General Kreat, the Boltbringer and Zada, Hedron Grinder are in the 99. THIS IS AN ELIMINATION, NEVER A WIN: we are at 5 life and seat-3 (36) and seat-4 (41) both remain, so killing seat-2 wins nothing.
steps.effect: Kill window: the combat damage step of turn 27, before our end step. Branch-only line. Best case is a one-seat elimination at a three-opponent table, with us the lowest life total in the game.

citations.quote: A turn consists of five phases, in this order: beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat main, and ending.
A player still in the game wins the game if that player’s opponents have all left the game.

steps.action: Declare attackers. We choose all TEN of our creatures and announce seat-2 as the defending player for each: Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3 Legendary Creature - Goblin Ally), Hanweir Garrison (2/3 Human Soldier), General Kreat, the Boltbringer (2/2 Legendary Creature - Goblin Soldier), five 1/1 Human Tokens and two 1/1 Goblin Tokens. All ten are listed untapped on the board; scenario-facts your_board.creature_bodies lists exactly these ten and spent_paying_a_cost is empty. Seat-3's Abaddon (5/5) is tapped and no opponent is attacked but seat-2. TWO PREMISES THE LIFT CANNOT CONFIRM, both recorded in extras.reconstruction_notes: (i) summoning sickness is not reconstructed (null on every body), so the declaration assumes each of the ten has been under our control since the turn began; (ii) both Goblin Tokens carry the annotation that their controller is INFERRED because the log never named one. Premise (ii) is the only live token uncertainty on this board and step 12 prices it.
steps.effect: Ten attackers against seat-2. DECLARED POWER = 3 + 2 + 2 + (5 x 1) + (2 x 1) = 14. (Stack 008 read this board as 8 attackers for 12 declared power; it was lifted by a bridge that omitted the two Goblin Tokens, and 14 supersedes 12.)

citations.quote: The chosen creatures must be untapped, they can’t also be battles, and each one must either have haste or have been controlled by the active player continuously since the turn began.
A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began.
the active player announces which player, planeswalker, or battle each of the chosen creatures is attacking.
a player can also choose to attack only one player during a particular combat.

steps.action: Attack triggers trigger, at the moment of declaration and only then. Hanweir Garrison: 'Whenever this creature attacks, create two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking' - it is a declared attacker, so this triggers ONCE. General Kreat's first ability: 'Whenever one or more Goblins you control attack, create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token that's tapped and attacking' - four Goblins are declared attackers (Zada is a Goblin Ally, Kreat a Goblin Soldier, and both Goblin Tokens are Goblins), but the trigger condition reads 'one or more' and one declaration of attackers is ONE trigger event, so it triggers ONCE, not once per Goblin. Kreat's second ability does NOT trigger here: nothing has entered yet. Both triggers are ours; we put them on the stack in whatever order we like before we get priority. WE CHOOSE Kreat's first trigger on the BOTTOM and Hanweir Garrison's on TOP, so Garrison's resolves first. The order changes no total below - it only fixes the interleave the question's 'Comprehensive Rules order' asks to see.
steps.effect: Two triggered abilities on the stack: Hanweir Garrison's (two Human tokens) on top, General Kreat's first (one Goblin token) beneath it. Four attacking Goblins still produce exactly one Goblin token.

citations.quote: Abilities that trigger on a creature attacking trigger only at the point the creature is declared as an attacker.
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.
Any abilities that triggered on attackers being declared or that triggered during the process described in rules 508.1 are put onto the stack before the active player gets priority
each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose.

steps.action: Resolve the top trigger, Hanweir Garrison's: create two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking. The creating effect does not name a defending player, so we choose one per token as it enters: seat-2 for both. These tokens are 'attacking' but never 'attacked', so neither Hanweir Garrison's attack trigger nor General Kreat's first trigger fires again off them - there is NO loop here, and the official rulings on both cards say the same thing (Hanweir Garrison, 2025-01-24; General Kreat, 2024-11-08). General Kreat's FIRST trigger is still on the stack, unresolved. The two Human tokens entering causes General Kreat's SECOND ability to trigger twice, and a triggered ability goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority and becomes the topmost object - i.e. on top of Kreat's first trigger. That is why both drains resolve BEFORE the Goblin token exists.
steps.effect: Two 1/1 red Human tokens enter tapped and attacking seat-2. Attackers 10 -> 12, power attacking 14 -> 16. Kreat's first trigger still on the stack, now beneath two of Kreat's entry triggers.

citations.quote: If a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking, its controller chooses which defending player, planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking as it enters the battlefield
The ability becomes the topmost object on the stack.

steps.action: Seat-4's Blind Obedience, checked once for all three tokens this line mints. Its oracle text is 'Extort (Whenever you cast a spell, you may pay {W/B}. If you do, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain that much life.) Artifacts and creatures your opponents control enter tapped.' We are its controller's opponent, so the second clause is a replacement effect modifying how our tokens enter. But every token here is already created 'tapped and attacking' by the ability that makes it, so applying Blind Obedience yields an identical result. Blind Obedience says nothing about attacking, and it is rule 508.4 (step 4) that makes these creatures attacking, so their attacking status is untouched. Its extort half triggers only when ITS controller casts a spell, and seat-4 casts nothing in this line.
steps.effect: Blind Obedience is INERT here: zero power, zero damage, zero life difference. The tokens were entering tapped anyway and remain attacking.

citations.quote: Some replacement effects modify how a permanent enters the battlefield.

steps.action: Resolve General Kreat's second ability, twice - the two triggers the Human tokens caused. Its text is 'Whenever another creature you control enters, General Kreat deals 1 damage to each opponent.' It does not target and it hits EACH opponent, so each resolution deals 1 to seat-2, 1 to seat-3 and 1 to seat-4; damage dealt to a player by a source without infect is life loss. PER-OPPONENT VERSUS POD, which are not interchangeable (scenario-facts drain_arithmetic, 3 opponents): each resolution is 1 per seat and 3 across the pod.
steps.effect: Two resolutions: 2 damage to EACH opponent, 6 across the pod. seat-2 17 -> 15, seat-3 36 -> 34, seat-4 41 -> 39. Our own life is untouched at 5.

citations.quote: Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.
its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.

steps.action: NOW General Kreat's first trigger resolves from the bottom of the stack: create one 1/1 red Goblin creature token that's tapped and attacking, and we choose seat-2 as the player it is attacking. That token entering triggers Kreat's second ability a THIRD time, which resolves for 1 more damage to each opponent. Nothing else triggers: the Goblin token is 'attacking' but never 'attacked' (step 4), and Boggart Shenanigans reads 'Whenever another Goblin you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield' - no Goblin of ours has died, so it has contributed nothing so far.
steps.effect: Third token enters. Attackers 12 -> 13. NON-COMBAT DAMAGE TO seat-2 THIS TURN = 3 (three creature entries x 1), and 9 across the pod - 3 per seat, never 9 per seat. seat-2 17 -> 14, seat-3 36 -> 33, seat-4 41 -> 38.

citations.quote: Similarly, if an effect states that a creature is attacking, its controller chooses which defending player, planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking (unless the effect has already specified).
causes that player to lose that much life.

steps.action: State the totals for part (a), and say what is and is not uncertain about them. Thirteen attackers are now attacking seat-2: Zada 3/3, Hanweir Garrison 2/3, General Kreat 2/2, seven 1/1 Human Tokens (five declared plus two minted) and three 1/1 Goblin Tokens (two declared plus one minted). Combat damage is assigned equal to power, so the power total is the figure that matters. READING extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions CORRECTLY: it records you: 4, which is the count of ALL token-creating resolutions our seat had in the log, NOT a count of tokens the lift left off the board. The seven tokens on this board are the product of those resolutions; the figure licenses adding NOTHING. (A previous pass misread it as four unlisted tokens and overstated a floor about fourfold.) This board is the RE-LIFT on the fixed bridge, so 17 is the total for the board as lifted, not a floor. The one residual uncertainty runs the other way and is priced in step 12: the two declared Goblin Tokens' controller is INFERRED.
steps.effect: (a) TOTAL POWER ATTACKING seat-2 = 17 across 13 attackers, before the Goblin Burrows pump; NON-COMBAT DAMAGE to seat-2 = 3, taking it from 17 to 14 life. Pod-wide non-combat damage = 9 (3 per seat).

citations.quote: Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power.

steps.action: HOLD Goblin Burrows until the declare blockers step, AFTER blockers are declared. Its text is '{1}{R}, {T}: Target Goblin creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn'; it taps as part of the cost, so it is available exactly once, and we have three Mountains plus Fountainport and Reliquary Tower untapped to pay {1}{R} (mana.open 6). It is a LAND, so the summoning-sickness rule of step 2 does not restrict it. An activated ability may be activated any time its controller has priority, and the active player gets priority in the declare blockers step once blockers have been declared - so the pump lands after seat-2 has committed its block and cannot be blocked around. We aim it at an UNBLOCKED Goblin (either declared Goblin Token, the minted one, or General Kreat).
steps.effect: +2/+0 on an unblocked Goblin in the declare blockers step: total power attacking seat-2 17 -> 19, all of the +2 unblocked.

citations.quote: A player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority.
Second, the active player gets priority.

steps.action: Part (b), first half: WHAT CAN BLOCK. Seat-2 controls two creatures. Reclamation Sage (2/1 Elf Shaman) is untapped and can be declared as a blocker. SPLINTERFRIGHT IS TAPPED - a field on this board, not an inference - and the declaration of blockers requires that each chosen creature be untapped, so seat-2 CANNOT declare Splinterfright as a blocker. THAT IS THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT, and it makes Splinterfright's size irrelevant. ITS POWER IS UNKNOWN, NOT ZERO: the board records */* because Splinterfright's power and toughness are set by a characteristic-defining ability ('Splinterfright's power and toughness are each equal to the number of creature cards in your graveyard') and the log carries no value for it. A DISAGREEMENT WORTH RECORDING: the lift gives seat-2 an empty graveyard, which for a turn-27 Jarad graveyard deck is a reconstruction gap rather than a reading - if it were literally true Splinterfright would be 0/0 and already in the graveyard as a state-based action, which would leave seat-2 with one creature. We do not resolve that disagreement, because the answer does not depend on it: tapped is tapped, and 0/0 is dead. Splinterfright's trample is likewise irrelevant, being a blocked-creature ability it never gets to use. Seat-2 also has no open mana (all three lands tapped, mana.open 0) and per the scenario we assume nothing castable in its five-card estimated hand.
steps.effect: Exactly ONE legal blocker: Reclamation Sage. Splinterfright cannot block whatever its size is, so no figure below depends on the unknown */*.

citations.quote: The chosen creatures must be untapped and they can’t also be battles.
Characteristic-defining abilities function in all zones.
If a creature has toughness 0 or less, it’s put into its owner’s graveyard.

steps.action: Part (b), second half: SEAT-2 TAKES ITS MOST FAVOURABLE BLOCK. With one blocker, blocking removes exactly the blocked attacker's power from the damage going to the player, so seat-2 maximises the power it blocks. Enumerating every block available to it: block Zada (removes 3), block Hanweir Garrison or General Kreat (removes 2), block any 1/1 token (removes 1), or decline to block (removes 0). Its best is to block ZADA, 3 power - and blocking Zada is also the choice that avoids a second problem: if Reclamation Sage (2/1) instead blocks a 1/1 Goblin Token, the Sage kills it and Boggart Shenanigans ('Whenever another Goblin you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may have this enchantment deal 1 damage to target player or planeswalker') triggers, so that block removes 1 combat damage and hands back 1 non-combat damage. Against the Zada block Boggart Shenanigans contributes ZERO: the Sage deals 2 to a 3/3 and Zada survives, while Zada's 3 kills the Sage - an Elf Shaman, and none of our own Goblins dies anywhere in this line. Because we held Goblin Burrows to step 9, the block is locked in before the +2 exists and the pump goes on an unblocked Goblin.
steps.effect: Most favourable block: Reclamation Sage blocks Zada, Hedron Grinder. Zada assigns its 3 to the Sage (which dies); the Sage assigns 2 to Zada (a 3/3, which survives). UNBLOCKED POWER = 19 - 3 = 16 going at seat-2's face.

citations.quote: An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s attacking.
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it.

steps.action: Combat damage step: all assigned damage is dealt at once. Seat-2 is at 14 life after the three Kreat drains and takes 16 from twelve unblocked attackers. A player at 0 or less life loses the game as a state-based action, checked the next time a player would get priority - which is within the combat damage step, long before our end step. ROBUSTNESS, EVERY NUMBER RE-DERIVED FOR THIS BOARD: (i) the line as played deals 16 against 14, margin 2; (ii) if we blunder and pump BEFORE blockers, seat-2 blocks the pumped 5-power Goblin and takes 19 - 5 = 14 against 14 - still exactly lethal (this is where stack 008's board differed: at 15 total power, pumping early left seat-2 alive, and on the corrected board it does not); (iii) with NO pump at all, 17 - 3 = 14 against 14 - exactly lethal; (iv) if premise (ii) of step 2 is wrong and neither declared Goblin Token is ours, declared power is 12, the total is 15, Kreat's trigger still fires once off Zada and Kreat, and the held pump gives 15 - 3 + 2 = 14 against 14 - exactly lethal; (v) if the board's TAPPED flag on Splinterfright were wrong and it could also block, two blocks remove 3 + 2 = 5 and 19 - 5 = 14 against 14 - exactly lethal, whatever its unknown power, since a block removes the ATTACKER's power and nothing of the blocker's. Every branch kills seat-2; only the margin moves. AND IT IS STILL AN ELIMINATION: seat-2 leaves the game and its permanents go with it, while seat-3 at 33 and seat-4 at 38 play on against us at 5 life.
steps.effect: (b) YES - seat-2 is dead in the combat damage step of turn 27, before our end step, taking its most favourable block: 14 life, 16 damage, -2. Seat-2 is ELIMINATED, we do not win, and we face two opponents on 33 and 38 from 5 life with our board tapped out from attacking.

citations.quote: all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously.
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
When a player leaves the game, all objects (see rule 109) owned by that player leave the game

final_state.summary: Thirteen attackers, 17 power (19 after the held Goblin Burrows pump), attack seat-2; three creature entries drain General Kreat's 1 damage to each opponent three times, 3 per seat and 9 across the pod, taking seat-2 from 17 to 14. Splinterfright is TAPPED, so under CR 509.1a it cannot be declared as a blocker and its */* - UNKNOWN, not zero, since the log carries no value for its characteristic-defining power - is irrelevant to every figure. Reclamation Sage makes the most favourable block, on Zada (3 power), and 16 unblocked damage kills seat-2 at 14 life in the combat damage step, before our end step. The kill survives every variant we could price: pumping early, not pumping, losing both inferred Goblin Tokens, or letting Splinterfright block anyway all still land exactly lethal. THIS IS AN ELIMINATION, NOT A WIN: seat-3 (33) and seat-4 (38) remain and we are on 5 life. The line needs Hanweir Garrison and is reachable on the zada-v1 BRANCH list only, not on goblin-storm's sleeved 99.

findings.note: MISSING STEP: the beginning of combat step is never walked. The resolution goes from precombat main (step 1) straight to declare attackers (step 2). CR 500.2 + 507.2 give every player a priority round in the beginning of combat step before attackers are declared, and the artifact never states the assumption that no opponent responds. It is not free: seat-3 has 3 open mana, seat-4 has 2 plus Blind Obedience's extort, and seat-2's open mana is understated (see the 509.1a finding) - and we are at 5 life. The kill on seat-2 survives, but the step and its assumption are absent.

MISSING STEP: no state-based action is checked for the blocking creature's death. Step 11 asserts 'Zada's 3 kills the Sage' and step 12 asserts Zada 'survives' with 2 damage marked, but 704.5g - 'If a creature has toughness greater than 0, it has damage marked on it, and the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed' - is never cited. 704.5f (toughness 0 or less) is cited, for a different creature in a hypothetical. The Reclamation Sage (2/1) taking 3 and Zada (3/3) taking 2 are both 704.5g questions.

MISSING STEP: step 12 asserts the 0-life check is 'checked the next time a player would get priority - which is within the combat damage step' and cites only 704.5a. The rule that establishes WHEN state-based actions are checked is 704.3 ('Whenever a player would get priority ... the game checks for any of the listed conditions'), read with 510.3 ('Third, the active player gets priority'). The timing claim - which is what makes the kill land before our end step - is uncited.

THE PREMISE IS FALSE AND THE LIFT IS STILL SHORT A PERMANENT. Step 10 states 'Seat-2 controls two creatures'. It controls THREE at the cut. Lord of Extinction (Creature - Elemental, */*, power and toughness equal to the number of cards in all graveyards) was milled into seat-2's graveyard and reanimated by Rise of the Witch-king ('you may return another permanent card from your graveyard to the battlefield'); it attacked our seat twice (10 combat damage, then 18 on turn 25) and was exiled by seat-4's Grasp of Fate on TURN 28 - after this turn-27 cut. It is on seat-2's battlefield at the cut and the re-lifted board omits it, which is the same class of defect (a silently omitted permanent, and again a '*/*' creature) that superseded stack 008. Verified in the run the scenario names: part-02.log, game 15 of the job, the Grasp of Fate zone change sits below the 'Turn: Turn 28' marker. 509.1a is the correct rule and the conclusion 'exactly one legal blocker: Reclamation Sage' survives - but only because the omitted creature attacked on turn 25 and is therefore also tapped, a fact the artifact cannot have relied on because it does not know the creature exists. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME STEP: 'SPLINTERFRIGHT IS TAPPED - a field on this board, not an inference' contradicts extras.reconstruction_notes, which says 'tapped creatures are those that attacked since their controller's last untap step; vigilance is not visible in the log'. The flag IS an inference. It happens to be right (Splinterfright attacked turn 25 and has only Trample), but the artifact denies a stated reconstruction limit it is leaning on. THIRD: 'Seat-2 also has no open mana (all three lands tapped, mana.open 0)' is false. Wight of the Reliquary resolved 'searches their library for a land card, puts it onto the battlefield tapped' before the cut; the bridge registers lands only from 'Land:' lines, so that land is missing and seat-2 has a FOURTH land, untapped as of turn 25's taps (Forest, Deathcap Glade, Woodland Cemetery only). Seat-2 has one open mana and five cards in hand, and 'no open mana' was offered as the reason the hand cannot matter.

THE LOG DOES CARRY THE VALUE. The artifact says four times that Splinterfright's size is unknown because 'the log carries no value for its characteristic-defining power' and 'must not be computed from here', and step 10 declines to resolve the graveyard disagreement. Splinterfright is 5/5 at the cut, measured twice in the very log the scenario cites: on turn 25 'Splinterfright (38) deals 5 combat damage to Ai(3)-mm-goblin-storm-zada-v1', and on turn 29 it assigned exactly 1 damage to each of five blocking Human Tokens (total 5) and was destroyed by their 5 damage, so power = toughness = 5. The only mills between the cut and turn 29 are Arcane Signet and Command Tower (Splinterfright's upkeep) and Cultivate, Svogthos the Restless Tomb and Necroblossom Snarl (Ripples of Undeath) - no creature card among them - so the turn-27 value is the same 5. The graveyard-is-a-floor caveat is right that the empty list must not be used; the inference drawn from it, that the size is unresolvable, is wrong, and it is what licenses leaving the 0/0 disagreement open. 604.3 is correctly applied to the CDA characterisation itself; the quote chosen ('function in all zones') is the sentence of 604.3 least relevant to the claim being made.

THE ROBUSTNESS CLAIM IS NOT EXHAUSTIVE AND OVERSTATES ITSELF. Step 12 prices five variants and concludes 'Every branch kills seat-2; only the margin moves'. Each is priced IN ISOLATION, and three of the five land on EXACTLY 14 against 14 life - zero slack - so any two adverse variants together fall short and 704.5a does not apply. On the artifact's own board: (iii)+(v) no pump with Splinterfright blocking = 17-5 = 12; (iv)+(v) = 15-5+2 = 12; (ii)+(v) pump early on Zada with two blockers = 19-7 = 12; (iii)+(iv) = 15-3 = 12; (ii)+(iv) = 17-5 = 12. All five leave seat-2 alive on 2. On the CORRECTED board variant (v) fails ON ITS OWN: if the tapped flags are wrong they are wrong for both turn-25 attackers, so three creatures could block and remove 3+2+2 = 7, giving 17-7+2 = 12. Variant (iv) is also internally incomplete - it assumes two mis-assigned Goblin Tokens vanish, when a mis-assignment moves them to another seat; if they were seat-2's and untapped they are two more blockers, 15-5+2 = 12. So 'all land at >=14 against 14, still lethal' is false, and 'holding the pump is now margin rather than a requirement' is true only of the single unstacked branch: the held pump is the ONLY branch with any slack (16 vs 14). Note also that variant (iv) is a hedge against nothing - the log names our seat as the creator of both Goblin Tokens (turn 23: 'Resolve Stack: Krenko's Command (215) - Ai(3)-mm-goblin-storm-zada-v1 creates two 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens'), so the 'controller is inferred' annotation is wrong for them.

SIBLING COMPARABILITY, recorded because scenario-facts is explicit and the charter is categorical: comparable_siblings marks 008 'DIFFERENT body count - do NOT quote its totals against this board', and step 2 quotes 008's '8 attackers for 12 declared power' while step 12 uses its '15 total power' as an arithmetic premise inside the robustness argument. This is the mildest finding in the set: 008 and 010 are two lifts of ONE cut (same run, game 61, turn 27), not two boards, and the artifact states what differs and in which direction, which is what a supersession note should do. The fix is one sentence - label 008 as the superseded LIFT OF THIS CUT rather than leaving scenario-facts' sibling flag standing against it.
Phase order establishes that the combat phase precedes the ending phase that holds our end step.
